content:
Match report as Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli in the Champions League at the Etihad Stadium.

Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang twice put the Italian side in front but equalisers from Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki earned Enzo Maresca's men a point Rayan Cherki’s late strike salvaged a 2-2 draw for Manchester City at home to Napoli in the Champions League but Enzo Maresca’s side again struggled to find their fluency.

Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund opened the scoring for the Italian side and though Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised, Noa Lang's volley stunned the Etihad Stadium as Napoli restored their lead late on.

Cherki's goal at least secured a point.

The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet.

title: "We made it unnecessarily difficult": Raum, Nusa, and returning Haidara react to Leipzig's 3-1 win over Lens
summary: RB Leipzig boosted their UEFA Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 3-1 victory over RC Lens at the Red Bull Arena on Tuesday evening, surviving a spirited second-half push from the French visitors after
content:
RB Leipzig boosted their UEFA Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 3-1 victory over RC Lens at the Red Bull Arena on Tuesday evening, surviving a spirited second-half push from the French visitors after racing into a two-goal lead inside the opening nine minutes.

Speaking after the final whistle, Leipzig captain David Raum - who opened the scoring in the sixth minute - praised his side's dominant first-half display while acknowledging that they lost control after the interval.

"We made it unnecessarily difficult for ourselves in the second half," Raum admitted.

"They're an important three points today - it was really important for us to get the win here, even if it wasn't flawless.

It can't always go like it did recently in the Bundesliga with five goals a game." Raum nonetheless took positives from how Martin Demichelis' side started the match and how the bench helped see out the closing stages.

title: "Gadou is just a beast!": Beier and Schlotterbeck reflect on Dortmund's hard-earned draw at Arsenal
summary: Borussia Dortmund walked away from the Emirates Stadium with a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday evening, bouncing back from an early deficit through Maximilian Beier'
content:
Borussia Dortmund walked away from the Emirates Stadium with a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday evening, bouncing back from an early deficit through Maximilian Beier's 55th-minute equalizer.

Speaking after the match, Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck admitted that his side made life difficult for themselves before the break before tightening up in the second half.

"I think in the first half we played too sloppily at times and gave away too many balls unnecessarily in attack," Schlotterbeck said.

"We did that better in the second half." Arsenal still carved out plenty of openings, though Schlotterbeck credited Dortmund's last-ditch defending - and voiced frustration over a second-half penalty appeal that went unpunished.

"Arsenal had a lot of chances, but we were also able to block many big opportunities," the center-back noted.

title: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30
summary: The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marque
content:
The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle.

According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings.

The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2.

Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters.

Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot.

title: Bayern hold constructive talks with Musiala's representatives amid ongoing tensions
summary: Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage. As per Sky Germa
content:
Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage.

As per Sky Germany, Musiala's agents Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschäffl met with Jan-Christian Dreesen, Herbert Hainer and Max Eberl at Säbener Straße on Tuesday, with neither Uli Hoeneß nor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge - both of whom have publicly raised concerns over Musiala's situation in recent weeks - present at the meeting.

The discussions are said to have been constructive, with both parties keen to improve communication behind closed doors following the recent public exchanges.

Having made his return to action against Köln on Friday, it is said that Musiala will now be given time to focus on his football, with the Bayern hierarchy keen to alleviate some of the pressure on the 23-year-old.

In the meantime, the attacking midfielder may have to take on a more integral role, with Harry Kane's absence, the unavailability of Michael Olise, and doubts over Luis Diaz ahead of the trip to Lille on Wednesday.

title: Lazio ultras temporarily lift Stadio Olimpico boycott but not everybody agrees
summary: ROME, ITALY - AUGUST 16: SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 remembered Livio Berruti with a minute's silence prior the Coppa Italia match between SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 at Stadio Olimpico on August 16, 2026 in Rome,
content:
ROME, ITALY - AUGUST 16: SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 remembered Livio Berruti with a minute's silence prior the Coppa Italia match between SS Lazio and Mantova 1911 at Stadio Olimpico on August 16, 2026 in Rome, Italy.

(Photo by Marco Rosi - SS Lazio/Getty Images) Ultras of Lazio’s Curva Nord have announced that they will temporarily lift their Stadio Olimpico boycott for their Serie A clash at home against Atalanta on December 6, but not all supporters agree with the decision.

Lazio supporters have been boycotting their home matches since the beginning of the calendar year in protest of owner Claudio Lotito.

Fans are demanding that Lotito sell the club and had promised that they would not return to the stadium, aside from derby fixtures, until he had done so.

Despite home season tickets plummeting to around 3,000 season and away supporters regularly outnumbering home fans in the Stadio Olimpico in 2026-27, Lazio have surged to the top of the Serie A table and remain unbeaten after the first 12 league matches of the season.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Juventus are on the hunt for a new centre-forward heading into the January transfer window, and Tuesday’s reports indicate that there are four leading candidates, including Atalanta’s Gianluca Scamacca.

Juventus could make several moves in January, including for a new central midfielder and full-back, but a new, physically dominant centre-forward is one of the biggest priorities.

Luciano Spalletti has recently spoken about his need for a traditional no.9 capable of playing with their back to goal, which neither Randal Kolo Muani nor Nick Woltemade really offer.
